page: OVHcloud t2-le-90 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance configured with 30 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6226R processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The host environment provides 90 GB of system memory, scaling at 3.0 GB per core, and is bundled with a 500 GB local NVMe SSD. For specialized parallel compute workloads, the instance integrates two NVIDIA Volta V100S graphics processors delivering an aggregate 64 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM, backed by a 4 Gbps baseline network connection.

Benchmark data positions the system as a strong platform for transformer model execution. In large language model evaluations, the dual V100S deployment attains top-decile performance across prompt processing and token generation across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models, reaching 1,423 tokens per second on 7B prompt ingestion. In contrast, CPU-centric metrics reflect middle-tier baseline compute, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,696 and a PassMark CPU score of 36,761.32. PassMark memory testing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both place within the top 25% of tested configurations.

The physical core implementation runs without hyperthreading, ensuring dedicated CPU scheduling per execution thread without resource contention. Architectural tradeoffs center on the contrast between high accelerator capacity and standard peripheral capacity, characterized by moderate network bandwidth and 500 GB of NVMe disk space. The platform offers efficient resource density for GPU-bound tasks without requiring oversized host memory tiers. The instance profile is aligned with deep learning inference, batch model evaluation, and accelerated parallel data processing pipelines.

It is well-matched for transformer model inference, parallelized computer vision jobs, and general machine learning evaluation workloads requiring substantial accelerator memory.
